idiom_name: ActiveJob + database-backed adapter (GoodJob / Delayed::Job / Solid Queue)
implementation_notes: In Rails the spool is the jobs table: a database-backed Active Job adapter serialises the payload into a row, a worker process forwards it, and the adapter's retry machinery plays the forwarder role - retry_on with a polynomial wait keeps the row and retries until the peer answers, and perform_later is the accept point. The classic hand-written spool (a directory of payload files plus a rake-driven drainer) is justified when no job backend exists, or when the payload is a large binary/stream that should not live in a database column. Broker clients such as bunny cover only the AMQP hop, so the in-process :async backend is never the store.
code_sketch:
class ForwardMessageJob < ApplicationJob
  queue_as :outbound
  retry_on Net::OpenTimeout, wait: :polynomially_longer, attempts: 25
  def perform(id, payload)
    Delivery.send!(payload)     # raises while the peer is unreachable
    Spool.delete(id)            # only after the peer acknowledged
  end
end
ForwardMessageJob.perform_later(msg.id, msg.payload)   # persisted in the jobs table
pitfalls: The :async and :inline adapters keep jobs in memory - they are not store-and-forward and lose accepted work on restart.
Enqueueing before the enclosing database transaction commits loses the job when the transaction rolls back (and can duplicate it on retry): use after_commit or the adapter's transactional support.
Permanent failures need discard_on/dead-letter handling; an unbounded retry list with no attempts cap turns one bad payload into a permanently failing queue.
Serialisation limits: huge or non-serialisable arguments should be stored by reference (an id or a file path) rather than inlined into the job row.
